categories.label: PET plastic bottle
steps: Empty the bottle completely and rinse with a little water.
Remove the cap and label — caps are collected separately as HDPE.
Crush the bottle flat to save space.
Take to a plastic buy-back hub; you can be paid per kilogram.

categories.label: Nylon / pure water sachet
steps: Shake out any water and let the sachet dry.
Bundle sachets together in one larger bag — loose nylon blocks drains.
Drop at a plastic buy-back hub that accepts nylon.
Never burn nylon: it releases toxic fumes.

categories.label: Food / kitchen waste
steps: Keep food waste separate from plastics and metals.
Compost at home in a shaded pit or bin, layering with dry leaves.
Turn the pile weekly; use finished compost on your garden after 6–8 weeks.
Alternatively drop at the community compost site.

categories.label: Electronic waste
steps: Back up and wipe any personal data from the device.
Remove batteries and keep them separate.
Do not burn or break the casing — it releases lead and mercury.
Deliver to the e-waste collection point for certified dismantling.

categories.label: Battery
steps: Tape the terminals of lithium and button cells to prevent short circuits.
Store in a dry, non-metal container away from children.
Never place batteries in household bins or open fires — they explode and leach acid.
Hand over at the e-waste collection point.

categories.label: Glass bottle or jar
steps: Rinse out residue and remove metal or plastic lids.
Keep whole bottles intact — they are worth more for reuse.
Wrap broken glass in thick paper and place in a sealed labelled box.
Deliver to the glass and bottle depot.

categories.label: Metal can / scrap metal
steps: Empty and rinse the can.
Flatten cans to save space (watch the sharp edges).
Collect until you have a few kilograms.
Sell at the scrap metal yard — aluminium pays best.

categories.label: Paper / cardboard
steps: Keep paper clean and dry — oily or wet paper is rejected.
Flatten cartons and remove tape and staples.
Bundle and tie with string.
Take to the paper and carton recycler.

categories.label: Clothing / textile
steps: Wash and dry the items.
Separate wearable clothing from worn-out fabric.
Donate wearable pieces; worn fabric becomes industrial rags.
Drop at the textile reuse point.

categories.label: Medical / sharps waste
steps: Place sharps in a rigid puncture-proof container (a thick plastic bottle works).
Never flush medicine down a toilet or drain.
Keep sealed and labelled 'MEDICAL WASTE'.
Hand over at the specialist hazardous waste intake — call ahead.

categories.label: Paint, solvent or pesticide
steps: Keep the product in its original labelled container.
Never pour into drains, soil or waterways.
Store upright, away from heat and children.
Deliver to the hazardous waste intake point.
reuse: Share unused paint with community projects

categories.label: Construction rubble
steps: Separate rebar and metal for the scrap yard.
Crushed concrete can be reused as hardcore for compaction.
Never dump rubble in drainage channels or on roadsides.
Arrange a licensed haulier for large volumes.

categories.label: General non-recyclable waste
steps: Bag securely so it does not scatter.
Place in your household bin for the scheduled collection day.
Do not burn — open burning releases dioxins.
Keep it out of drains and open plots.
